what: float64 Gauss-Newton step on a uniform tensor grid on [-1, 1)^D for separable networks u(x) = sum_r prod_d phi_d(x_d)_r (one tanh MLP 1 -> width -> ... -> R per axis, widths 48 / 64 / 96, depths 3 / 4 / 5), linear L with constant or separable coefficients and a separable target: loss, gradient g = J^T Q r and 10 fixed conjugate-gradient iterations on (J^T Q J + lam I) x = g, lam = 1e-6 g.g / P, identical CG code for every method; candidate = omnibias.jax.experimental.separable_grid.separable_grid_gauss_newton (the Jacobian-vector product of the rank-J CP residual is a rank-DJ CP tensor; J^T Q J v from per-axis J x J mixed Gram matrices and one JVP / transpose of the derivative-table map; grid never materialised)
hardware: one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (exclusive), JAX 0.10.2 with jaxlib 0.10.2 CUDA 12 plugins, CPython 3.12

protocol.repetitions: 3 fresh processes (paired by repetition, rotating method order)
protocol.statistic: ratio = strongest-control median / candidate median per tier; lower95 = exp(mean(log r) - 2.920 sd(log r)/sqrt(3)); strongest control = smallest mean log median among qualified tier members
protocol.qualification: every method's (loss, gradient, Gauss-Newton product) operator on the 3^D (2^D when 3^D > 64) sub-grid of the first nodes vs a 40-digit oracle (truncated Taylor series in x with dual parts along two fixed random parameter directions u, v): loss 1e-9 / 2e-10, g.v, v^T G v and u^T G v 1e-8 / 2e-9 (scaled). The CG iterate is not compared: 10 CG iterations on the damped near-singular system amplify 1e-15 product differences

status.parity: lower95 < 1 <= ratio or ratio < 1 <= upper bound
status.partial: an applicable tier member failed (e.g. out of memory) or did not qualify; never promoted

protocol.fairness: identical data, initialisation, loss and float64 inputs for every method; compilation excluded (value-and-gradient steady state)

tiers.explicit_grid_residual_gn: the same separable model and CG with Gauss-Newton products through the residual materialised on the N^D grid: the rank-J CP GEMM chain linearised once or re-differentiated per product, one outer product per operator term (the reference separable-network residual), or vmapped Taylor-mode tables
tiers.autodiff_mixed_gram: the same identity J^T Q J v = grad <r, sg(J v)>_Q and shared factor linearisation with the J x J Gram algebra differentiated by JAX

roles.held_out: cells and seed not used for any tuning

full_grid_accuracy.what: max over repetitions of per-field relative deviations (norms and sampled entries scaled by the largest sampled reference magnitude) between methods at full size; floor = two controls; loss and gradient only (the CG iterate is not an accuracy measure here: the two explicit grid controls differ from each other by up to 69% in it)

cold_cost.what: per cell, medians over repetitions: cold = lowering + compilation ms (excluded from the speed ratios), steady = steady-state median ms, for the candidate and the steady-state-fastest member of every tier; break_even_calls = extra cold ms / steady saving per call (only when the candidate compiles slower and runs faster)
